title: Flat-mop microfiber system with a charging bucket
audience: Cleaners who use a flat mop with microfiber pads and a charging bucket on hard floors in offices, commercial buildings and homes.
learningOutcomes: Load a charging bucket with the right amount of solution and the right number of pads.
Attach a pad to a flat mop, then use it so that the pad stays evenly damp.
Use the flat mop in the same order as a bucket mop, with the pad replaced when it is spent.

instruction.heading: What the flat system does differently
instruction.body: A flat mop carries a microfiber pad on a holder, and the pads are wetted in a charging bucket rather than a wringer. Microfiber pads trap soil in their fibres, so a clean pad lifts more soil with less solution. The system also means fewer hands-on steps: the cleaner does not twist the mop head by hand. The method is only as good as the pad, so the pad must be clean and the charging bucket must be set up correctly every time.

instruction.heading: Setting up the charging bucket
instruction.body: Add cold water to the charging bucket in the amount suited to the number of pads being used, following the marks on the bucket. Add pH-neutral floor detergent at the label dose. Load the pads with the white backing uppermost, so the microfiber side sits in the solution. Close the lid and fasten each flap so nothing spills in transit. Grip the bucket by its handle and move it firmly from side to side so the pads take up the solution evenly. Set the bucket down and open the lid when you are ready to mop.

instruction.heading: Mopping with the flat head
instruction.body: Set a telescopic handle to a height that suits you. Lower the holder into the bucket to take up a damp pad. The pad should be damp, not dripping. Stand upright, tackle the corners and edges before the open floor, then fill the open floor with a steady fanning motion, moving backward toward the exit. Keep the bucket on the unfinished side, behind you, so that you never walk on a section you have washed. Overlap each pass by a short distance. When the pad is saturated or grey, replace it, rather than rinsing it on the floor.

instruction.heading: Finishing the flat mop job
instruction.body: When the last area is complete, take the flat mop and the charging bucket back to the cleaning cupboard. Take out any unused pads, rinse them, squeeze them, and hang them up to air dry. Dirty pads go into a laundry bag. Dry the holder with a cloth. Rinse the bucket inside and out, dry it, and store it in its marked place. Remove the wet floor signs once the floor has dried.

procedure: Put on gloves and eye protection, and lift any floor mats before starting.
Scrape adhesive labels or chewing gum off the floor with a putty knife.
Set out wet floor signs by the room entrances.
Fill the charging bucket with cold water in the amount suited to the pads, and add pH-neutral floor detergent at the label dose.
Load the pads with the white backing uppermost, close the lid and fasten each flap so the seal is tight.
Move the bucket firmly from side to side, then set it down and open the lid.
Lower the holder into the bucket to take up a damp pad, then tackle the corners and edges before the open floor, then the open floor toward the exit in overlapping passes.
Replace the pad once it is saturated or grey, placing the spent pad in a laundry bag.
Return the flat mop and bucket back to the cleaning cupboard, rinse and store the pads, clean the bucket and mop, and remove the signs once dry.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner charges a bucket and begins mopping. Halfway across a large office the pad has turned grey, but the cleaner keeps going and rinses it in the sluice on the floor.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the cleaner have done, and what is the correct step now?
workedExamples.reasoning: A saturated pad spreads soil rather than lifting it. Replace the pad with a clean damp one taken out of the charging bucket, and keep the spent pad for laundering. Rinsing a pad on the floor puts the soil back onto clean surfaces.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner loads a charging bucket with a full set of pads but mixes the solution with extra cleaner, because the floor looked dirty.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the problem, and what should be done?
workedExamples.reasoning: Extra cleaner beyond the label dose can leave a film on the floor and make it slippery. Dose the solution to the label and the fill mark. If the floor still looks dirty, the soil may need a different method, so tell the supervisor.

equipmentAndPpe: Flat mop with a telescopic handle, where used.
Charging bucket with lid and side flaps.
Clean microfiber flat mop pads, with the white backing for the bucket.
pH-neutral floor detergent, dosed to the label.
Putty knife, broom or dust mop.

commonErrors.error: Using a grey or saturated pad until the floor shows a film.
commonErrors.prevention: Replace the pad as soon as it is no longer clean and damp.

commonErrors.error: Loading the pads with the microfiber side facing up, so they do not wet evenly.
commonErrors.prevention: Place the pads with the white backing uppermost, as the bucket layout requires.

commonErrors.error: Leaving the lid unsealed, so the solution spills on the way to the room.
commonErrors.prevention: Lock the lid and seal every side flap before moving the bucket.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Lift the charging bucket by its handle and keep the back straight. Ask for help with a full bucket if it is too heavy to carry safely.
Keep the wet floor signs in place until the floor has dried. Wear gloves and eye protection when dosing or handling the cleaner.

qualityStandard: Every pad used is clean and damp when it first touches the floor.
The floor is mopped in full, including corners and edges.
The floor has no film, streaks or residue once dry.
The charging bucket and flat mop are rinsed, dried and stored in their marked place.
documentationEvidence: Job record of the area mopped, with the product dose used and the date and time.
Note of the number of pads used and laundered for the job, where the site tracks pads.
summary: A flat mop uses a clean microfiber pad, damp and not dripping.
Dose the solution and set the pads with the white backing up, then seal the lid.
Tackle the corners and edges, then the open floor toward the exit.
Replace a saturated pad, and never rinse it on the floor.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do when a microfiber pad turns grey during mopping?
options: Rinse it on the floor and keep mopping with it until the floor is dry
Replace it with a clean, damp pad taken out of the charging bucket
Wring it harder and keep using it across the whole floor

knowledgeChecks.question: How should the pads be placed in the charging bucket?
options: With the microfiber side facing up, so the backing stays dry and clean
Folded into a ball so that they hold more solution and fit more of them in the bucket
With the white backing uppermost, so the microfiber side takes up the solution

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should the floor cleaner be dosed to the label?
options: Because too much product can leave a film and make the floor slippery
Because the label dose is the only way the pads will stay damp
Because extra product makes the pads last longer
